_note: Participation mystique: the definition (CW6 ¶781), the identity it names (CW10 ¶69, CW17 ¶83), the naming's reservation (CW10 ¶130), its clinical importance (CW10 ¶852), its reach into art and matter (CW15 ¶162, CW14 ¶336, CW5 ¶203), and the retraction Jung refused to follow (CW18 ¶345, the note beside Lévy-Bruhl's own diary). Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: Jung's definition of Lévy-Bruhl's term (CW6), his statements on what it means (CW10, CW17), its form between two people, and its occurrences in art, alchemy and the analogies of the unconscious.

sections.title: The definition
sections.line: CW6 ¶781 (Psychological Types, Definitions, 1921): Jung's definition of the term, which he attributes to Lévy-Bruhl; a footnote in CW18 (pdf p933) on Lévy-Bruhl's retraction.

quotes.quote: It denotes a peculiar kind of psychological connection with objects, and consists in the fact that the subject cannot clearly distinguish himself from the object but is bound to it by a direct relationship which amounts to partial identity (q.v.).

Lévy-Bruhl later retracted this term under the pressure of adverse criticism, to which he unfortunately succumbed. His critics were wrong inasmuch as unconscious identity is a well-known psychological fact.

sections.title: Identity, not sympathy
sections.line: CW10 ¶69 and ¶130 and CW17 ¶83: Jung's statements of what the term means, and of the word mystical.

quotes.quote: To put it briefly, it means a state of identity in mutual unconsciousness.
There is nothing “mystical” about identity, any more than there is anything mystical about the metabolism common to mother and embryo.
Lévy-Bruhl has coined the expression participation mystique for these remarkable relationships. It seems to me that the word “mystical” is not happily chosen.

sections.title: In the clinic
sections.line: CW10 ¶852: what Jung says happens when a dialogue between two people touches something fundamental, essential and numinous.

quotes.quote: It is an unconscious identity in which two individual psychic spheres interpenetrate to such a degree that it is impossible to say what belongs to whom

sections.title: In art, and in matter
sections.line: CW15 ¶162 on artistic creation, CW14 ¶336 on the alchemists and their substance, and CW5 ¶203, the vault note's earliest adoption of the term (Wandlungen, 1912).

quotes.quote: This re-immersion in the state of participation mystique is the secret of artistic creation and of the effect which great art has upon us
a state of participation mystique,662 or unconscious identity, arose between them and the chemical substance
In this way there came into being those intimate relationships by analogy which Lévy-Bruhl fittingly describes as “participation mystique.”
